se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli 1.3.0 发布, Companion command-line tool for VibeTags: `init` bootstraps a project's opt-in
        files (file presence is the opt-in signal the processor honours), `doctor`
        reports the project's VibeTags health — build-tool wiring, active platforms,
        marker integrity. Run it without installing anything:

            jbang se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-cli:1.3.0 init --list

        The platform list and marker rules are read from vibetags-processor, so this
        tool cannot drift from what the processor actually does.

se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom 1.3.0 发布, Bill of Materials for the VibeTags annotation processor. Import this BOM to get
        a coherent vibetags-annotations + vibetags-processor pair without specifying
        each version individually.

        Recommended setup — annotations on the compile classpath, processor on the
        annotation-processor path only (the processor jar pulls in slf4j/logback,
        which has no business on consumer code's compileClasspath):

        Maven:
            <dependencyManagement>
                <dependencies>
                    <dependency>
                        <groupId>se.deversity.vibetags</groupId>
                        <artifactId>vibetags-bom</artifactId>
                        <version>1.3.0</version>
                        <type>pom</type>
                        <scope>import</scope>
                    </dependency>
                </dependencies>
            </dependencyManagement>

        Gradle:
            implementation platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.3.0')
            annotationProcessor platform('se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-bom:1.3.0')
            compileOnly 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-annotations'
            annotationProcessor 'se.deversity.vibetags:vibetags-processor'

        @AIIgnore, @AIPrivacy, @AICore, @AIPerformance). Zero third-party dependencies.
        All annotations use RetentionPolicy.SOURCE so they leave no trace in the

            <dependency>

eu.jsentinel:jCustos-credentials-hibp 00.81.10 发布, Optional Phase-5 extension that adds a HaveIBeenPwned-style online
    compromised-password checker on top of the V00.71 SPI from
    jCustos-core. The checker uses the k-anonymity range API: only
    the first five hex chars of the candidate's SHA-1 digest leave the
    process, never the plaintext password (CWE-359). The implementation
    relies on JDK HttpClient only — no additional runtime dependencies.
    Strictly opt-in; applications that do not depend on this module
    perform no online lookups.

items.title:
org.wso2.carbon:org.wso2.carbon.http.bridge 4.12.52 发布, There are two ways to use OSGi in server-side[1].
        In Carbon, what we have done is, embedding an OSGi framework inside a servlet container.
        So BridgeServlet delegates all the request from the servlet container to the
        HttpServiceServlet registered by the http.bridge bundle. This is required only
        when Carbon is running inside a webapp.

        There is a possibility to embed an HTTP server(ex. jetty) inside equinox and
        start a server with all our carbon bundles. This is same as running carbon
        inside spring DM server. For this scenario, we do not need
        org.wso2.carbon.http.bridge bundles and the org.wso2.carbon.bridge extension bundle.

        1. http://eclipse.org/equinox/server/http_quickstart.php
